subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add a supported configurable permission policy for agent-created user-facing files, and which write paths and defaults are in scope?
rationale: The requested fix adds config surface and changes a local filesystem security boundary across core tool writes, so automation should not choose the permanent policy or default without maintainer intent.

options.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
options.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with explicit exclusions for sensitive state and coverage across host, apply_patch, sandbox, and exec-related write paths.

options.title: Use fixed per-path defaults
options.body: Avoid a new config knob and continue fixing concrete writer defaults, such as media-readable or workspace-document modes, where maintainers approve each boundary.

options.title: Document host setup only
options.body: Leave runtime permissions unchanged and document ACL, Docker user/group, umask, or NAS permission setup as the supported operator workaround.

recommendation.title: Approve scoped user-output policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrow tools/workspace-output permission policy with explicit exclusions for sensitive state and coverage across host, apply_patch, sandbox, and exec-related write paths.

likelyOwner.reason: This person has the strongest history across the schema, filesystem safety, host write, and sandbox mutation boundaries that need the product/security decision.
